decisions.reason: The concept is diversity across festivals. A single generic celebration icon would erase the distinction and could misteach the row.
The reviewed meaning is an unexpected event that may cause damage or injury. A single crash, fall, or broken-object icon would narrow the meaning to one accident type.
The reviewed meaning is having a lot to do. A single person or activity icon cannot express workload without adding a more specific scene than the semantic row warrants.
The reviewed verb means saying a question because an answer is wanted. A generic speaking-person icon would not distinguish asking from talking, telling, or answering.
The reviewed verb is deictic movement toward the speaker or referenced place. A static movement icon lacks the required viewpoint and could teach the wrong direction.
The reviewed meaning covers the place and surroundings where a person, animal, or plant lives. One habitat picture would incorrectly narrow this broad concept.
The meaning is the general category of things people wear. One garment icon would collapse the category to a particular item; a composed clothing-set visual should be authored separately.
The meaning is the sweet substance used in foods and drinks. A white-granule or bowl icon is visually ambiguous with salt and other powders without an authored contextual scene.
The reviewed adjective means extremely good. A star, trophy, or thumbs-up would encode praise rather than the lexical meaning and would not be semantically exact.
The reviewed adjective means very great or far beyond what is usual. Its visual form depends on the modified property, so one generic icon would be misleading.
The reviewed adjective means known through prior experience. Recognition depends on learner context and cannot be represented by a universal static object icon.
The reviewed adjective means known by many people. A celebrity or landmark icon would substitute an example for the lexical relation itself.
The reviewed adjective describes moving or happening very quickly. A static object would conflate the property with one fast thing; a motion-aware semantic scene belongs in the visual lane.
The reviewed noun is the flat walking surface at the bottom of a room. A generic room or ground icon would not isolate that surface; an authored room-part scene is needed for exact visual teaching.
The reviewed noun is a person whose role is watching a place or person to keep them safe. A generic person or uniform icon does not establish the protective role.
The reviewed noun is a person who shows others where to go or what to do. A generic person icon cannot distinguish a guide from other people without a role-specific scene.
The reviewed noun is a place where books and other reading materials are kept for people to use. The existing book icon represents a book, not the place-and-service meaning of library.
The reviewed noun is the duration of 60 seconds. The existing generic clock icon represents a clock, not one minute; a precise timed-state visual would be required.
The reviewed noun is an informational message. A paper, sign, or text icon would only show a medium and would not establish that the content is a notice.
The reviewed verb is moving something by drawing it toward you or in a direction. A correct visual needs a source, object, direction and motion state rather than a static generic arrow.
The reviewed adjective means happening in a usual or repeated way according to a pattern. The property depends on a sequence over time and cannot be represented by one static object icon.
The reviewed adjective means unusual or different from what is expected. Any single odd-looking object would encode one subjective example rather than the lexical meaning.
